sentences.text: Revenue compounded 6.2% a year from $26.6 billion in FY2016 to $45.7 billion in FY2025 [F1][F10][F157], but the path was a cycle, not a line.
Revenue rose 25.6% in FY2018 to $37.4 billion [F3][D93], with the Wirtgen acquisition adding 12% to net sales that year [P72].
Revenue then climbed 23.9% in FY2021 to $44.0 billion [F6][D231] and 16.5% in FY2023 to $61.3 billion [F8][D322], before falling 15.6% in FY2024 [D367] and 11.7% in FY2025 [D412].

The FY2024 decline came as rising global grain stocks, lower commodity prices and elevated interest rates cut shipment volumes [P17], and FY2025 volumes fell 30% in U.S. and Canada large agriculture [P10].
Production Agriculture was the largest driver, at 37.1% of FY2025 revenue [D657], and it subtracted 7.0pp from FY2025 growth [D659].
Construction & Forestry was 25.5% of revenue [D889] and subtracted 3.0pp [D891], while Financial Services grew to 13.8% of revenue [D922].
The FY2025 Production & Precision Agriculture volume drop of 30% in the U.S. and Canada was only partly offset by a 22% increase in Brazil [P10].
Operating income grew 16.9% a year FY2016..FY2024 against 6.2% revenue growth [F159][F157], but FY2025 operating costs fell 7.3% against an 11.7% revenue decline [D425][D412].
Diluted EPS fell 27.8% in FY2025 against a 29.2% net income decline [D415][D413], as the diluted share count fell 1.9% [D427].
The FY2024 operating margin of 17.5% [F30] sat 5.4pp above the 12.1% window median [D1335], but was 3.7pp below the FY2023 high of 21.2% [F29][D378].
The FY2024 margin fell 3.7pp, with SG&A costing 1.9pp and R&D 0.9pp [D378][D391][D390].
FY2024 production costs were favorable on lower material and profit-sharing costs, partly offset by higher overhead from lower volumes [P16].
The FY2025 net margin of 11.0% [F50] was 2.7pp lower than FY2024 [D422] and 5.6pp below the FY2023 high of 16.6% [F48][D1337].
The FY2025 effective tax rate was 20.1% [D400], and net margin trailed operating margin by 3.7pp in FY2024 [D1373].
Operating cash flow of $7.5 billion was 1.48x net income in FY2025 [F80][F40][D401], above the 1.17x window median [D1364].
Free cash flow was $6.1 billion, a 13.4% margin [F100][D398], against a 11.6% window median [D1341].
FY2025 operating inflows were driven by net income adjusted for non-cash provisions and a decrease in sales receivables [P5].
Capex of $1.4 billion was 3.0% of revenue and 0.61x D&A [F90][D397][D403].
Cash was $8.3 billion at FY2025 [F140], up 13.0% [D420], against $13.8 billion of current debt [X185].
Long-term debt is not reported after FY2021 [X191], so net cash and debt growth across the break are omitted here [R9].
Return on average equity fell to 20.6% in FY2025 [D411], in the 17th percentile of six industrials peers against a 28.3% median [D1361][D1362].
Buybacks plus dividends of $2.9 billion were 46.9% of free cash flow [D409][D410], and the diluted share count fell 1.9% [D427].
Revenue fell in both FY2024 and FY2025 [F9][F10][R1], a two-year decline after the FY2023 peak.
Production Agriculture, 37.1% of revenue, fell 17.6% in FY2025 [D657][D658][R2], and Construction & Forestry, 25.5% of revenue, fell 11.8% [D889][D890][R4].
Small Agriculture & Turf operating profit fell on lower volumes and higher tariffs, partly offset by price realization [P8].
The allowance for credit losses rose in FY2025 on higher expected losses in agriculture and turf accounts [P4], with the provision at $296 million [X171].
Long-term debt is missing after FY2021 and current debt before FY2020 [R9][R10], so net-cash comparisons across those breaks are unreliable.
If FY2026 revenue falls again from the FY2025 level of $45.7 billion [F10], the two-year decline becomes a third year; the FY2026 10-K will show it.
Watch whether the operating margin recovers toward the 12.1% window median [D1335] from the FY2024 level of 17.5% [F30] in the FY2025 10-K.
Watch free cash flow against the $6.1 billion FY2025 level [F100], given guidance for lower FY2026 equipment operating cash flow [P6].
